name: Sonnet dividend growth and income
strategy: Anchor in quality dividend growers with AI-cycle exposure, add a tactical short against the most overextended leveraged momentum trade, use TLT for rate-cut convexity, and keep meaningful cash at 4% APY given stretched valuations after a huge H1 rally.

positions.thesis: Azure past $100B annualized revenue growing 41-43%, 2026 capex raised to $175B, Maia 300 AI chip reveal coming this fall; durable AI-driven cash flow anchoring the dividend book, unchanged.

Trimmed after a 5.94% single-day drop (vs flat SMH/NVDA) tied to China domestic chip competitiveness headlines (CXMT Shanghai debut) and Goldman pulling it off its Conviction List -- the exact China-headline risk this thesis already flagged as a watch item is now showing up in price. Apple's >$30B multi-year deal and the Samsung $200B foundry/memory tie-up keep the long-term AI-silicon franchise intact, so keeping a reduced stake rather than exiting.
Just printed a fresh record high ($34.52, +30% over the past year) as capital rotates toward dividend-payers; diversified quality dividend-growth ballast, kept as core holding.
Trading at $362.84, within 1% of its $366.50 52-week high; best-in-class rising-dividend compounder, no thesis break.

$200, +1.16% today, still riding record Q2 earnings (net income +385% YoY) with a 25-analyst Buy consensus and $216.83 PT; energy dividend aristocrat remains the book's inflation/rate-backdrop diversifier.

The catalyst cluster -- 'Micron and other chip stocks fall as China steals the spotlight' on CXMT's strong Shanghai debut (a domestic Chinese memory/foundry competitiveness story), Goldman pulling AVGO off its US Conviction List on 8/2, and an EU antitrust loss on the VMware documents request -- is exactly the China-competition/headline risk this book's AVGO thesis already flagged as a watch item, now actually manifesting in price and news rather than sitting as a hypothetical. Everything else confirms as-is: MSFT (Azure AI franchise intact, Maia 300 chip coming this fall), SCHD (fresh record high $34.52, +30% 1yr), JPM ($362.84 vs 52wk high $366.50), CVX ($200, +1.16%, record Q2 earnings still the story), HD/TLT unchanged because 30-year yields are pushing toward 5.1% and 'yields will go much higher next year' headlines confirm the rate-cut convexity case for TLT/HD still hasn't arrived, XLP unchanged defensive ballast. Trimming AVGO into cash rather than rebuilding the rest of the book, consistent with the mandate's instruction to keep meaningful cash given stretched valuations.
